title: Mouse Without Borders sometimes blocks at screen edge unless clicking desktop while switching PCs
author: Lusiiky

judgment.rationale: The intermittent edge block matches the more specific open #41849 fullscreen-detection issue: clicking the desktop helps, and adding explorer.exe to ignored fullscreen applications is reported to fix it. This report should be consolidated there unless a current test disproves the link.
evidence: The cursor sticks at the edge primarily when moving from the host PC.
Clicking the desktop can allow switching.
A commenter reports that adding explorer.exe to ignored fullscreen applications completely fixes the same behavior.
Issue #41849 describes Easy Mouse being disabled on the windowless desktop by fullscreen detection.
judgment.recommended_action: Link this report to #41849 and continue the fullscreen-detection fix there.

fix_assessment.rationale: The public workaround and matching trigger point to an existing canonical issue rather than an independent fix.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders edge switching can be blocked because the desktop shell is treated as fullscreen; explorer.exe exclusion is a reported workaround.
known_information: The failure is intermittent and asymmetric.
No fullscreen app is intentionally running.
The explorer.exe ignored-fullscreen workaround is reported effective.
inferences: This is likely the same fullscreen-detection defect tracked by #41849.
issue_context.analysis: Consolidation preserves the stronger cause-oriented report and avoids parallel design work.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the current public issue body, labels, assignees, and up to the latest 20 public comments returned by GitHub.
Kept the existing dashboard read-only; no dashboard files were modified or published.

actions.label: Consolidate with #41849
actions.note: Draft candidate only; no comment or other write was made to microsoft/PowerToys.

comment.body: This appears to match #41849: Easy Mouse can be disabled while the desktop shell is active because explorer.exe is treated as fullscreen. The reported workaround of adding `explorer.exe` to Ignored fullscreen applications reinforces that link. Please consolidate the fix investigation in #41849 unless current testing shows this edge-blocking case still occurs with fullscreen disabling turned off.
